title: Incremental output TTL, resume handshake, and disconnect reconciliation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: clients frequently disconnect during long generations (mobile networks, tab backgrounding). Current behavior leaves partial generations and KV-prefix state indefinitely, which increases memory footprint and confuses later resume attempts. Goal: implement a deterministic TTL-based garbage collection for partial outputs and a symmetric resume handshake that guarantees no-dupe or missing-token conditions while preserving SLOs for time-to-first-token and tail latency. This ticket scopes: (1) server-side partial-output TTL with conservative defaults and per-route override, (2) lease-based resume handshake between client and server to validate prefix continuity, and (3) client disconnect classification (transient vs terminal) to choose retain-vs-gc policy.
acceptance_criteria: Partial outputs (ephemeral generation fragments) annotated with server-generated lease_id and expires_at are evicted automatically when TTL passes
Resume handshake protocol: client presents last_ack_cursor + optional resume_token; server verifies lease_id lineage and either allows resume or returns a deterministic fallback response
Telemetry: histograms emitted for partial_gc_latency, resume_success_rate, resumed_time_to_completion; dashboards added to Console
Default TTL config 2 minutes with per-route override via API and Console; system respects Dedicated and Private deploy policies
Automated unit + integration tests covering normal disconnect, flaky reconnect (network churn), and client replay attack scenarios
design_decisions: Use server-issued lease_id on first partial chunk instead of relying solely on client-provided resume_token to avoid token forgery
TTL is conservative by default (2m) to balance memory vs usability; Dedicated customers can set higher retention
On resume mismatch, server returns a canonical fallback generation (short deterministic message) and flags a regression event for model-eval pipelines
KV cache entries tied to lease_id are soft-marked and eligible for eviction after TTL; hard eviction only after grace period to avoid KV cache churn during transient network blips
implementation_notes: Server: add lease_id and expires_at fields to PartialOutput proto, persist meta in the ephemeral store used by generator workers
Router: on client reconnect, validate last_ack_cursor -> lookup lease_id lineage in ephemeral store; if lineage absent, return 410-style resume-failed payload with suggestion to restart generation
Client SDKs: add resume_handshake helper that retries with exponential backoff jitter and surface explicit is_resumable boolean to callers
Metrics: instrument resume_attempt, resume_success, partial_gc_count, lease_conflict_count; tag by route/model/deployment
Config: expose per-route partial_ttl_seconds and resume_grace_seconds in API schema and Console UI
open_risks: Race between background GC and late-arriving reconnect causing resume false-negatives; mitigated by short grace window and conservative defaults
Potential spike in storage ops when many aborted sessions produce short-lived leases; will monitor partial_gc_count and add batching to cleaner if needed
Compatibility: older SDKs without resume_handshake could still reuse naive resume_token; plan to return clear upgrade path and 1-month compatibility mode
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease lifecycle: creation, extension, expiration, manual revoke
Fault-injection integration tests simulating flaky networks and duplicate reconnects using chaos harness
Performance test measuring added latency on first-token for canonical route at QPS 1000 (must be < 3ms median impact)
E2E test from SDK: generate long response, simulate client disconnect, reconnect with resume_handshake and assert resumed content continuity
